R101.note: getHost()!=null plus opaque-absolute check restricts sendRedirect to relative/local paths; Java's URI parser rejects backslash bypass attempts up front (verified), so the check is not trivially bypassable.

R102.note: Adds a real server-side IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync check matching the AuthorizeView role gate; requires the 'AdminOnly' policy to exist in Program.cs but the write-up states this explicitly rather than hiding it.

R103.note: Uses JNDI's parameterized search(name, filterExpr, filterArgs, cons) overload, which escapes filter args per RFC 4515; passing new SearchControls() is documented as equivalent to the original null argument, so behavior is unchanged.

R104.note: Regex allowlist [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ structurally prevents any traversal sequence from reaching require(); the accompanying path.relative/startsWith double-negation check is confusing and effectively dead code (regex already blocks dots/slashes) but is not itself harmful.

R105.note: allowed_classes restricted to ShoppingCart::class blocks gadget-chain instantiation while preserving the wire format and the existing instanceof/default-cart fallback for legitimate cookies.

R106.note: Controller-side allowlist of the four legit columns plus created_at default satisfies the stated contract; tenantId binding and mapper untouched.

R107.note: GET->POST plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken is the standard CSRF fix; the write-up openly updates the confirmation view to a POST form with an antiforgery token so legitimate use is not silently broken.

R108.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the exact pattern used by every sibling route; no other observable change.

R109.note: Fix references message.UserId, but ChatMessage only defines AuthorUserId - as written this does not compile, so the ownership check is never applied.

R110.note: Regex allowlist on username prevents LDAP metacharacters from reaching the filter; matches the repo's established C# CWE-90 allowlist pattern (no built-in LDAP filter escaper exists in System.DirectoryServices).

R111.note: snprintf with return-value checks rejects oversized input instead of truncating, and the final 'AUDIT %s' output preserves the exact original format and return-code contract.

R112.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 correctly HTML-encodes the untrusted note with no other observable change.

R113.note: Contract requires the default created_at sort remain available, but none of the proposed hardcoded methods sort by created_at; the shown findForTenant signature also drops the sort parameter that InvoiceService.listInvoices still calls with two arguments, so applied as shown it would not compile.

R114.note: archive/tar reading removes the shell entirely, a strong fix, but silently drops support for gzip-compressed archives that GNU tar -tf auto-detects (tar.NewReader alone cannot read .tar.gz), an unstated behavior regression for any legitimate compressed archive.

R115.note: Uses the file-type library's detected.ext (content-derived) instead of the client-supplied extension, correctly reconstructing the dot-prefixed filename; no other observable change.

R116.note: Replacing Process.Start/PowerShell with System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping fully eliminates the shell sink, but the response body format changes from PowerShell's native Test-Connection output to a synthesized one-line string, a substantive content change not called out as a deliberate side effect.

R117.note: Content-based finfo MIME check plus a fully server-generated random filename removes both the dangerous-extension and path-traversal vectors; client-supplied name is never used again.
